mainTopic: מתעסק on שבת: the מחלוקת between אביי and רבא, and the גמרא's analysis of the ברייתא comparing שבת to other מצוות, which turns out to mean עבודה זרה.
overview: The גמרא first rules that someone who only meant to lift a detached plant, and accidentally cut an attached one, is פטור. Then אביי and רבא disagree about someone who meant to cut a detached plant and cut an attached one instead: רבא says פטור, and אביי says חייב. רבא brings a ברייתא as proof. It says that in other מצוות, 'שגג בלא מתכוין' is חייב, but on שבת it is not. Before using the proof, the גמרא works out the ברייתא's first line. It concludes that 'other מצוות' means עבודה זרה, following רבי אמי. The גמרא then looks for a case of 'שגג בלא מתכוין' in עבודה זרה. Bowing in a supposed בית הכנסת fails, and so does bowing to a statue. Bowing out of love or fear works only for אביי. The case of one who thinks it is 'מותר' clashes with רבא's own question to רב נחמן. The answer to that challenge comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Meant to lift a detached plant but cut an attached one
steps.stepSummary: Someone who meant only to lift a detached plant, and accidentally cut one still attached to the ground, is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he meant to lift a detached plant and instead cut an attached plant, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a basic ruling: if a person had no plan to cut at all, an accidental cut is not counted as a sin on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person never meant to do any cutting. He only wanted to pick something up. That makes him a מתעסק, someone not really doing the act on purpose, so he does not bring a קרבן חטאת.

phrases.english: If he intended to lift a detached plant,
and he cut an attached plant, he is exempt.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who had no intention to cut at all is a מתעסק and is פטור.

steps.title: Meant to cut a detached plant: אביי and רבא disagree
steps.stepSummary: If he meant to cut a detached plant (which is permitted) and cut an attached one, רבא says פטור and אביי says חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he meant to cut a detached plant and cut an attached plant: רבא says he is exempt, אביי says he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a harder case, where the person did mean to cut, just not this plant. אביי and רבא disagree about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case differs from Step 1 because here he planned an act of cutting. The question is whether planning to cut something permitted is enough to make the accidental forbidden cut count as a real שוגג.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 1. In Step 1 he wanted to lift, not cut, and everyone agrees he is פטור. The מחלוקת here is only because he did want to cut.

phrases.english: If he intended to cut a detached plant,
and he cut an attached plant,
Rava said: he is exempt.
Abaye said: he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: לַחְתּוֹךְ אֶת הַתָּלוּשׁ, וְחָתַךְ אֶת הַמְחוּבָּר, רָבָא אָמַר: פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a case everyone agrees on to a disputed case that is close to it.

steps.title: The reasons behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he never meant a forbidden cut. אביי says he did mean to cut, and that is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says exempt, because he did not intend a forbidden cutting. אביי says liable, because he did intend cutting in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each side of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that on שבת you must intend a forbidden act, and cutting a detached plant is not forbidden. אביי holds that intending the general act of cutting is enough, so the actual cut counts as a normal שוגג.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the main question of the sugya: what kind of intention does שבת require for a person to be liable?

phrases.english: Rava said exempt,
because he did not intend a forbidden cutting.
Abaye said liable,
because he did intend cutting in general.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר פָּטוּר — דְּהָא לָא מִיכַּוֵּון לַחֲתִיכָה דְאִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the מחלוקת from Step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא requires intent for a forbidden act. אביי is satisfied with intent for the act in general.

steps.title: רבא's proof from a ברייתא comparing שבת to other מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא: in other מצוות, 'שגג בלא מתכוין' makes you חייב, but not on שבת. This matches his case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? A ברייתא teaches that שבת is stricter than other מצוות in one way, and other מצוות are stricter than שבת in another way. שבת is stricter because two acts done in one lapse of awareness bring a separate obligation for each, unlike other מצוות. Other מצוות are stricter because there, one who acts unwittingly without intent is liable, unlike on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a source to support his view. He points to the ברייתא's second line, which says 'שגג בלא מתכוין' on שבת is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא understands 'שגג בלא מתכוין' as exactly his case: the person meant something permitted and accidentally did something forbidden. Since the ברייתא says this is פטור on שבת, it supports רבא against אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the two 'stringencies'. The first is about how many חטאות you bring. The second, the one רבא uses, is about intention.

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say this?
As it was taught: Shabbat is stricter than other מצוות in one way,
and other מצוות are stricter than Shabbat in another way.
Shabbat is stricter than other מצוות
in that on Shabbat, if he did two in one lapse of awareness,
he is liable for each and every one,
which is not so with other מצוות.
And other מצוות are stricter than Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת שָׁגַג בְּלֹא מִתְכַּוֵּין — חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: in that with other מצוות, one who erred without intent is liable,
which is not so on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא supports his side of the מחלוקת with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that someone who meant to cut a detached plant and cut an attached one is פטור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: 'שבשאר מצות שגג בלא מתכוין חייב, מה שאין כן בשבת'.

steps.title: What case does the first line of the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's first line again and asks what case it is describing.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר said: שבת is stricter than other מצוות, because on שבת, two acts in one lapse of awareness bring a separate obligation for each, unlike other מצוות. What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: Before using the ברייתא for רבא's proof, the גמרא stops to understand its first line. It is setting up a test of possible cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the first line on purpose, because it is now examining it. The question is what situation would make שבת give two חטאות while other מצוות give only one.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: חוֹמֶר שַׁבָּת מִשְּׁאָר מִצְוֹת,
phrases.english: The Master said: Shabbat is stricter than other מצוות,
in that on Shabbat, if he did two in one lapse of awareness,
he is liable for each and every one,
which is not so with other מצוות.
What is the case?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: חוֹמֶר שַׁבָּת מִשְּׁאָר מִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps aside from the proof to examine the ברייתא's first clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case of two acts makes שבת give two חטאות while other מצוות give only one?

steps.title: Reaping and grinding cannot be the case
steps.stepSummary: If it means reaping plus grinding, the matching case is eating חלב plus דם, and both give two חטאות. So there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he did reaping and grinding, the matching case in other מצוות is eating חלב and דם. Here he is liable for two, and there he is liable for two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible case, two different מלאכות, and shows it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different מלאכות on שבת match two different איסורים, like חלב and דם. Both bring two חטאות, so the ברייתא's claim that שבת is stricter would not be true.

keyTerms.meaning: forbidden fat and blood (two different איסורים)

phrases.english: If you say he did reaping and grinding,
the matching case in other מצוות
is that he ate forbidden fat and blood.
Here he is liable for two,
and here he is liable for two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a first answer to the question in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא's first line as reaping plus grinding.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The matching case in other מצוות also brings two חטאות, so no stringency of שבת is shown.

steps.title: Repeating the same act cannot be the case either
steps.stepSummary: If it means eating חלב twice, the matching case is reaping twice, and both give one חטאת. Again there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is the case in other מצוות where he is liable for only one? Where he ate חלב and again חלב. The matching case on שבת is reaping and reaping again. Here he is liable for one, and there he is liable for one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the opposite approach, the same act repeated, and that fails too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating one איסור in one lapse of awareness gives one חטאת. Repeating one מלאכה on שבת also gives one חטאת. Both cases still come out equal, so neither reading shows a stringency of שבת. The next step answers this with 'לעולם'.

phrases.english: Rather, in other מצוות

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא מִיחַיַּיב אֶלָּא חֲדָא הֵיכִי דָּמֵי —
phrases.english: where he is liable for only one, what is the case?
Where he ate forbidden fat and forbidden fat.
The matching case on Shabbat
is where he did reaping and reaping.
Here he is liable for one,
and here he is liable for one!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁאָר מִצְוֹת דְּלָא מִיחַיַּיב אֶלָּא חֲדָא הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first case fails, tries the opposite case, which also fails.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as the same act repeated.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both שבת and other מצוות give only one חטאת for a repeated act, so again no difference.

steps.title: Answer: reaping and grinding, compared to עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The case really is reaping and grinding. 'Other מצוות' means עבודה זרה, following רבי אמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is where he did reaping and grinding. And what does 'which is not so with other מצוות' mean? It refers to עבודה זרה, following רבי אמי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first case, reaping and grinding, and explains that 'other מצוות' refers specifically to עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not comparing שבת to every מצוה. It is comparing it to עבודה זרה, where several different acts of worship in one lapse bring only one חטאת. Different מלאכות on שבת each bring their own חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: actually, really (going back to an earlier option)

steps.confusionAlert: 'לעולם' tells you the גמרא is going back to the case it rejected in Step 6. It keeps that case and changes the meaning of 'other מצוות'.

phrases.english: Actually, it is where he did reaping and grinding,
and what is 'which is not so with other מצוות'?
It refers to idolatry,
and in line with Rabbi Ami.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problems of Steps 6 and 7 by narrowing what 'other מצוות' means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of a phrase in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Other מצוות' means all other איסורים, so no case shows a difference.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Other מצוות' means עבודה זרה, where several different acts in one lapse bring only one חטאת.

steps.title: רבי אמי: several acts of עבודה זרה bring only one חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rules that someone who sacrificed, burned incense, and poured a libation to an idol in one lapse of awareness brings only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי אמי said: If he sacrificed, burned incense, and poured a libation in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אמי's ruling, which is the source behind the answer in Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though these are different acts of worship, in one lapse of awareness they count as one חטאת in עבודה זרה. On שבת, different מלאכות count separately. That is the stringency of שבת the ברייתא means.
steps.whatToRemember: The first line of the ברייתא means: different מלאכות on שבת each bring a חטאת, while different acts of עבודה זרה in one lapse bring only one, following רבי אמי. The next step tests this עבודה זרה reading against the ברייתא's second line, about שגג בלא מתכוין.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ami said:
If he sacrificed, burned incense, and poured a libation
in one lapse of awareness,
he is liable for only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Different acts of עבודה זרה in one lapse of awareness bring only one חטאת.

steps.title: Does the idolatry explanation fit the ברייתא's last line?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the עבודה זרה explanation from the end of the ברייתא. That line says someone who acted 'שוגג without intent' is liable in other מצוות. What would such a case look like in עבודה זרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: You explained the ברייתא as talking about עבודה זרה? Then look at the end of it: 'A stricter point in other מצוות: in other מצוות, one who acted by mistake without intent is liable, which is not so on שבת.' What would a mistaken, unintended act of עבודה זרה look like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new explanation against the ברייתא's last line. It asks what an accidental, unintended act of עבודה זרה would even be. This sets up the next few attempts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'other מצוות' means עבודה זרה, then the second half of the ברייתא must also be about עבודה זרה. It says one who is 'שוגג without intent' is liable there but exempt on שבת. The גמרא needs a real case of this in עבודה זרה, and it is not obvious that one exists.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you explain it? (In what case did you set it?)
Look at the last part (of the teaching)
Acted by mistake without intending the act
What is the case? What does it look like?

steps.confusionAlert: On שבת, an act done 'without intent' (מתעסק) brings no חטאת at all. The ברייתא says other מצוות are different. The question is whether עבודה זרה can be one of those different cases.

phrases.english: In what case did you set it — in idolatry?
Then say the last clause:
A stricter point in other מצוות:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת שָׁגַג בְּלֹא מִתְכַּוֵּין — חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: that in other מצוות, one who erred without intent is liable,
which is not so with Shabbat.
This 'erred without intent'
in idolatry, what is the case?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתַּהּ — בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה? אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 8 by testing it against the ברייתא's last clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that 'other מצוות' means עבודה זרה (step 8).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא is about עבודה זרה, there must be a case of 'שוגג without intent' in עבודה זרה that makes one liable. It is unclear what that case could be.

steps.title: Bowing in what he thought was a synagogue is no sin
steps.stepSummary: First attempt: he bowed to what he thought was a בית הכנסת, and it was really an idol's house. This is rejected because his heart was turned to Heaven, so he did nothing wrong at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he thought it was a בית הכנסת and bowed to it, that does not work. His heart was directed to Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one possible case of accidental עבודה זרה and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who bows while meaning to serve ה' has not served an idol, even by mistake. So there is no sin and no חטאת. That cannot be the ברייתא's 'liable' case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
His heart is directed to Heaven

phrases.english: If you say: where he thought it was a synagogue
and bowed to it,
his heart was toward Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 10's question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case of mistaking an idol's house for a בית הכנסת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His intent was for Heaven, so there is no sin, not even an accidental one.

steps.title: Bowing to a statue is either deliberate or meaningless
steps.stepSummary: Second attempt: he bowed to a king's statue. If he accepted it as a god, he sinned on purpose, which is not a שוגג. If he did not, his bow means nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say he saw a statue and bowed to it. What is the case? If he accepted it as a god, he sinned on purpose. If he did not accept it as a god, it means nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second case, bowing to a statue, and shows that it fails either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case splits into two options. Accepting the statue as a god makes him a מזיד, and a מזיד brings no חטאת. Not accepting it means the bow is only respect for the king and not עבודה זרה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted it upon himself as a god

phrases.english: Rather, where he saw a statue and bowed to it,
what is the case?

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּקַבְּלֵהּ עֲלֵיהּ בֶּאֱלוֹהַּ — מֵזִיד הוּא.
phrases.english: If he accepted it upon himself as a god, he is a deliberate sinner.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי דְּלָא קַבְּלֵהּ עֲלֵיהּ בֶּאֱלוֹהַּ — לָאו כְּלוּם הוּא.
phrases.english: And if he did not accept it as a god, it is nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 11 fails, offers a second case and rejects it with a two-sided argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case of bowing to a king's statue.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Either he meant it as worship, which makes him a מזיד, or he did not, which makes it no act of עבודה זרה at all. Neither is a liable שוגג.

steps.title: The case is bowing out of love or fear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is someone who bowed to an idol out of love or fear of a person. He did not truly accept it as a god, and he thought that made it allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is one who bowed out of love or out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new case that might fit the ברייתא: bowing because of love for, or fear of, another person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the person really did an act of worship, but without accepting the idol as a god. He mistakenly thought that without real belief it is not forbidden. This is a middle ground between the two failed options of step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Out of love (for a person) and out of fear (of a person)

phrases.english: Rather, out of love and out of fear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10's question after steps 11–12 failed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There seemed to be no case of a liable, accidental, unintended act of עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bowing from love or fear is such a case: a real act of worship, without true acceptance, done by mistake.

steps.title: This works for אביי but not for רבא
steps.stepSummary: The love-or-fear case fits אביי, who holds such a person liable. But רבא holds him exempt, so for רבא the problem remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for אביי, who said he is liable. But for רבא, who said he is exempt, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 13. It shows that the answer only works according to one side of a famous argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא argue about someone who bows to an idol out of love or fear. אביי says he brings a חטאת, so the ברייתא's 'liable' fits. רבא says he is exempt, so for רבא we still have no liable case.

keyTerms.meaning: What can be said? (the problem remains)

phrases.english: This works for Abaye, who said he is liable.
But according to Rava, who said he is exempt,
what is there to say?

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבא this person is exempt, so the case cannot be the ברייתא's 'liable' case.

steps.title: The case is one who thinks it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: New answer: the person thought עבודה זרה was permitted, and for this he is liable. On שבת, someone who thought מלאכה was permitted would be completely exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is one who says 'it is permitted.' 'Which is not so on שבת' means that there he is completely exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new case for 'שוגג without intent': a person who did not know the act was forbidden at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'without intent' means he had no idea it was a sin, because he thought it was permitted. In עבודה זרה he would be liable. The ברייתא's 'not so on שבת' is read to mean that on שבת such a person is fully exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: One who thinks (says) it is permitted

phrases.english: Rather, where he says 'it is permitted.'

phrases.aramaic: מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּשַׁבָּת דְּפָטוּר — לִגְמָרֵי.
phrases.english: Which is not so with Shabbat, where he is completely exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the love-or-fear answer, which failed for רבא in step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שוגג without intent' meant bowing out of love or fear, which fails for רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means one who thought the act was permitted. He is liable in עבודה זרה but completely exempt on שבת.

steps.title: רבא never considered total exemption on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 15 from רבא's question to רב נחמן. רבא only asked whether such a person brings one חטאת or two. He never thought the person might be completely exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא only asked רב נחמן whether to make him liable for one or for two. But to exempt him completely, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'thinks it is permitted' answer by pointing to an earlier question of רבא. That question shows such a person is not exempt on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא asked about a person who did not know about שבת and did not know the מלאכות. He asked whether this person brings one חטאת or two. That means he was surely liable for at least one, so the claim that on שבת he is 'completely exempt' contradicts רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Only this far did… (the question went no further)
To make him liable for one or for two (חטאות)

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer of step 15 now conflicts with רבא, the very opinion the גמרא was trying to satisfy. So the search for the right case must continue.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Rava only asked Rav Naḥman
whether to make him liable for one
or to make him liable for two,
but to exempt him completely — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that on שבת one who thinks מלאכה is permitted is completely exempt (step 15).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's question to רב נחמן assumed such a person is liable for at least one חטאת. So 'completely exempt' contradicts רבא.
